text:
Alex K: Heads-up — I ran a focused benchmark comparing synthetic traffic vs replay harness for KV-cache warmup and autoscale behavior. Posting summary + proposed follow-ups.

Maria R: nice, can you paste the commands & key numbers?

Alex K: sure. run command used:```./tools/replay_harness --trace ./traces/payment_flow.json --duration 20m --mode replay --concurrency 80 --record-kv-stats```and```./tools/replay_harness --synthetic --qps 1200 --duration 20m --seq-dist 'short:0.6,long:0.4' --concurrency 80```Key obs: p50 gen latency (hosted runtime) — replay: 32ms, synthetic: 28ms. p95 — replay: 180ms, synthetic: 95ms. KV hit-rate after 5m — replay: 78%, synthetic: 12%. Kernel selection (attn kernel A vs fallback B): replay picked A 86% of tokens, synthetic only 45% (because longer tail sequences triggered fallback).

Nora: wow the KV hit-rate diff is huge. That explains p95 gap. Were batching heuristics different?

Alex K: yes — synthetic requests had wider length variance so batching merged dissimilar seqs more often. Our dynamic batcher currently uses sequence-length bucketing with a ±8 token tolerance; with synthetic mix that tolerance allowed grouping short+long which forces kernel B and larger memory pressure. With replay, prefix locality kept batches homogeneous.

Samir: do we have profiler dumps? kernel time vs memory copy?

Alex K: attached outputs inline:```PROFILE SUMMARY (aggregate 20m replay) kernel_A_time: 12.4s kernel_B_time: 2.1s kv_lookup_time: 0.9s memcpy: 1.7s total_tokens: 23.4M```For synthetic:```kernel_A_time: 6.8s kernel_B_time: 7.3s kv_lookup_time: 3.8s memcpy: 4.5s total_tokens: 25.0M```Interpretation: synthetic workload forces more kernel_B and memcpy/KV overheads.

Ryan: interesting — so kernel selection policy + batching bucketing interact heavily with traffic shape. How did autoscale respond? scale-up time? cold start counts?

Alex K: autoscale summary (Dedicated pool, 8->32 gpus target): replay run triggered scale from 8->12 in 85s, 12->24 in 3m22s, stable at 24 until 7m then to 32 at 9m10s. Synthetic: 8->20 in 2m10s, 20->32 at 6m40s. Coldstart fail rates negligible, but warmup penalty higher in synthetic due to KV misses and repeated kernel fallbacks. Burst credits used: replay consumed 0.2 credits/min, synthetic 0.9 credits/min.

Maria R: can you correlate scale decisions with per-route p95? I want to know if we scaled too slowly for replay p95 spikes.

Alex K: correlation shows two spike windows at replay t+90s and t+200s where p95 jumped >300ms for ~40s before autoscale caught up. For synthetic the p95 was elevated but more stable (fewer sharp spikes) — likely because synthetic is steadier high QPS.

Nora: proposal: run a 3x repeat with (A) replay-only, (B) synthetic-only, (C) hybrid (real trace + jitter) and capture: kernel selection counts, batch size distribution histogram, kv-hit heatmap over time, and exact autoscaler decision logs. Also add a small experiment toggling batcher tolerance to ±4 and to size-aware grouping.

Samir: +1. Also instrument the runtime to emit per-batch "dominant seq length" metric so we can see how mixed the batches are.

Alex K: noted. I'll add `batch.dominant_len` and `batch.homogeneity_ratio` counters to the harness and runtime telemetry.

perf-bot: scheduled benchmark job 1773554321-1: runs in staging-dedicated pool, reserved 32 gpus, expect ~30m runtime. Link: https://ci.internal/runs/1773554321-1

Ryan: for apples-to-apples we need identical VMs, same model checkpoints (quantized vs fq), and kernel build flags. Please pin the kernel ABI.

Alex K: pinned to `kernel-1.9.3+opt` and model `redwood/open-7b:v2-quant` in the job config. Also disabled auto-quant fallback to avoid hidden differences.

Maria R: what's the acceptance criteria? what would we change in production?

Alex K: short-term: tighten batch tolerance for pool types serving interactive traffic to ±4; add pre-warm of KV caches when scaling up (proactively request prefixes from checkpoint up to 10k tokens). Medium-term: update kernel selector to prefer kernel_A when avg batch homogeneity_ratio > 0.7, even if memory footprint is just borderline.

Nora: pre-warm approach — do we prefetch to KV on pod creation? we need to watch memory pressure and avoid extra OOMs.

Alex K: prefetch will be rate-limited and only for dedicated pools with spare memory headroom flag. We'll run a safety test first.

Samir: thanks Alex. Can you attach the raw histograms and the per-batch logs to the CI run? I'll start a flamegraph pass on kernel_B code path.

Alex K: yeah will upload artifacts to CI. Tentative schedule: reruns tomorrow 10:00 PT, collect 3 repeats each, then sync Friday.

Ryan: sync added. @Maria R @Nora please review the job config before 10am.

Maria R: ack :thumbsup:

Nora: thanks, will review.

Alex K: closing notes: key takeaway — benchmark shape (synthetic vs replay) drastically changes batch homogeneity and kernel selection which drives KV hit-rate and p95 behavior; autoscaler timings interact with spikeiness — we need both better warmup and smarter batcher heuristics for production SLOs.
